title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: An agent run has made five model calls. Why does the fifth call cost more to read than the first, even if the fifth tool result is tiny?

options.text: The program resends the earlier messages, so the fifth call reads all of them
The model remembers the earlier calls and must reread its own memory
Later calls are always billed at a higher rate per token than the first
The window shrinks with each call, so the model reads each token twice

items.stem: A student finishes laser-cutter training on Tuesday. On Thursday, in a brand-new session, the assistant must know this. Which design makes that reliable?

options.text: Trust the model to recall Tuesday, since it was told once already
Save the status in a database and load it when the session starts
Enlarge the context window so that Tuesday's session still fits inside
Write the status into the system prompt of the model's training data

items.stem: Ignoring the system prompt and tool descriptions, a student's question is 100 tokens and the program makes two tool calls, each result 600 tokens. Counting only the question and the two results, how many tokens does the model read on its final call, which writes the answer?
Your team proposes pasting all twelve machine manuals into the system prompt of every request, since the model's window is large enough to hold them. What is the best objection?

options.text: Large windows are an error; the request would be refused outright
The model would forget the manuals after the first answer it gives
Every call would pay for all that text, and recall may worsen
The model cannot read text placed in a system prompt at all

items.stem: In one or two sentences: when the assistant answers a question using a manual, what does retrieval put into the context, and what does it leave out?
